title: Does Your App Need an Admin Panel? How to Manage Content and Users Without a Developer

cards.heading: List what changes after launch
cards.text: Prices, photos, offers and opening times. If it changes often, you need a way to edit it.

cards.heading: Choose one of three levels
cards.text: Developer changes, simple content editing, or a full admin panel. Each is more useful and more work.

cards.heading: Name who makes the changes
cards.text: A named person and a back-up, not "the team". A tool only helps if someone uses it.

cards.heading: Give each person only what they need
cards.text: Limit who can see customer details, and remove access promptly when someone leaves.

cards.heading: Keep the accounts in your name
cards.text: Hosting and databases should be yours, with your developer given access. Confirm it in writing.

facebook.message:
Who changes a price or a photo in your app once it is live?
Most app planning focuses on what customers see, not who manages it afterwards. Our new guide explains what an admin panel does, three levels from developer-only changes to a full back office, and the questions to settle before you build, such as who makes changes and who can see customer details. Watch for the key points in the short video.

To read the full article, visit the FinTaxTech website and find "Does Your App Need an Admin Panel? How to Manage Content and Users Without a Developer" in our Blog section.
